subject: Post-call: trial scoping, scoring matrix & methodology choice (Cobalt Health)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Cho <amelia@cobalthealth.io>, Tom Nguyen <tn@cobalthealth.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-16T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next steps and scoring matrix

Hi Amelia / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposal for how Redwood and Cobalt Health can run a short, focused evaluation to get you comfortable with model quality, safety, and cost before a procurement decision.

Key needs you raised:
- High-confidence PHI redaction for clinical transcripts
- Sub-350ms p50 latency for autocompletion flows
- Consistent answer quality for summary tasks (abstraction & factuality)
- Predictable unit cost / ops profile for 100k–1M monthly requests

Proposed acceptance criteria (initial):
1) Quality score (aggregated rubric) >= 0.80
2) Redaction recall >= 0.95, precision >= 0.90
3) Avg inference latency p50 <= 350ms; p95 <= 800ms
4) Error rate (incorrect hallucinations flagged by human review) <= 5%
5) Estimated per-1M-token cost within your budget band (we'll model with real traces)

Evaluation approach (two complementary tracks):
- Offline evaluation (recommended first): Redwood runs reproducible offline runs on a de-identified subset you provide (~500 transcripts). We return a scoring matrix with per-task metrics (precision/recall for redaction, BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies for summaries, human-graded 1–5 quality). Advantage: fast, deterministic, repeatable; lower risk for PHI.
- Live shadow (optional second stage): 2-week shadow where model responses are logged and scored against live interactions (no user-facing changes). Advantage: captures real distribution and latency; downside: needs infra & governance sign-off.

Ownership & timeline (proposed):
- Cobalt: share de-identified sample set and existing human-eval rubric by 2026-05-18.
- Redwood: run offline eval, produce scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx and a short findings memo by 2026-05-20 (owner: Rishi).
- If both sides agree, aim to start a 2-week shadow no earlier than 2026-05-25 (infra checklist to be validated).

Attachments: scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx (template) attached — please review columns and weightings.

Open questions for you:
1) Are the proposed acceptance thresholds in the right ballpark? 
2) Do you prefer we weight safety/redaction higher than quality for the decision? If so, by how much (e.g., 60% safety / 40% quality)?
3) Do you have any compliance constraints we should factor before the shadow?

I suggest a 30-minute follow-up on Friday (2026-05-21) to lock timeline after you confirm dataset availability.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps and scoring matrix

Thanks Vanessa — good write-up and aligned on the approach. A few notes from our side:

- We can provide the de-identified sample set by EOD 2026-05-18. We'll strip direct identifiers and hash patient IDs. Our compliance lead will also include a short data provenance note.
- On the shadow: we prefer a 3-week window if feasible. That gives our clinical reviewers enough time to surface edge cases. If Redwood needs a 2-week minimal window to be practical, we can discuss a 2+1 model (2 weeks main + 1 additional week if triggers exceed thresholds).
- Regarding weights: safety/redaction should carry more weight in the final decision — proposing 65% safety / 35% quality. We are less price-sensitive in the short POC but want a clear cost projection.

One ask: can Redwood include a short section in the scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx that shows how false negatives on redaction map to patient-risk categories? That will help our CISO understand residual risk.

I'll loop in our CS partner after we confirm the timeline.

Amelia Cho

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps and scoring matrix

Adding technical detail based on today’s discussion and Amelia's notes. My proposed additions to the rubric and an updated scoring approach:

Rubric architecture (per item):
- Redaction (safety): measured as recall and precision on annotated tokens; map false negatives to risk buckets: low/med/high (we'll produce a short breakdown in redaction_metric_notes.md).
- Quality (accuracy/factuality): human raters score 1–5; aggregate mean and % >=4; also compute contradiction rate vs source docs.
- Latency: p50/p95 measured end-to-end including network; we’ll run using realistic traces you provide.

Scoring matrix (simple example):
- Safety score (0–1) = weighted avg of redaction recall (0.6) and redaction precision (0.4)
- Quality score (0–1) = normalized mean rater score / 5
- Composite score = 0.65 * Safety + 0.35 * Quality (per Amelia's preference)

Acceptance thresholds (suggested, can be tuned):
- Composite score >= 0.80
- Redaction recall >= 0.95
- Mean human rating >= 4.0 (on 1–5)
- p50 latency <= 350ms (note: this requires a dedicated routing profile; see infra-checklist.pdf)

Action items assigned:
- Redwood (Rishi): run offline runs and produce scoring outputs (owner). Deliverables: scoring_matrix_v1.xlsx, redaction_metric_notes.md, short results memo. ETA: 2026-05-20.
- Cobalt (Amelia): deliver de-identified sample + provenance note (ETA: 2026-05-18).
- Redwood infra (ops): validate shadow checklist and confirm whether shadow can run in staging without a dedicated VPC (see infra-checklist.pdf).

I attached redaction_metric_notes.md (explains tokenization caveats and edge-case mapping) and infra-checklist.pdf (pre-shadow controls). Once we have the dataset I’ll run a small pilot batch to give you an early indication.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — we have alignment on the plan. Quick summary of decisions and next steps so nothing falls through: 

Decisions: 
- Run offline evaluation first (Redwood/Rishi). Deliver scoring matrix + notes by 2026-05-20.
- If offline results meet minimal thresholds, run a 2-week live shadow with option to extend to a 3rd week if triggers appear.
- Weighting confirmed: 65% safety / 35% quality. Acceptance composite >= 0.80.

Owners & deliverables: 
- Cobalt (Amelia): sample dataset + provenance (due 2026-05-18) and assign a CS contact for shadow operations.
- Redwood (Rishi): offline runs, redaction notes, infra-checklist validation (deliver by 2026-05-20).
- Redwood (Vanessa): project lead, coordinate procurement paperwork and scheduling; I’ll pull in contracts once we get initial pass results.

Next meeting: Proposed 30-min sync to review scoring matrix on 2026-05-21 at 10:00 AM PT. If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

If no objections I’ll treat this as the agreed plan and proceed.

Thanks — looking forward to moving ahead.
